chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Wahb, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who left behind his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, he said: 'For the paternal aunt are two-thirds, and for the maternal aunt is one-third.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a paternal aunt versus a maternal aunt in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distribution of the estate when a deceased leaves only his paternal and maternal aunts, assigning two-thirds to the paternal aunt and one-third to the maternal aunt. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it demonstrates the application of the 'two shares for males, one for females' principle adapted to female collateral relatives, distinguishing their shares from those of uncles. The hadith highlights the specific hierarchical precedence of the paternal line in inheritance calculations when no closer male or female heirs exist.
